name: Creamy Razor Clam Chowder
description: A creamy New England-style chowder made with razor clams, sized for a 3-quart pot.

ingredients.item: chopped razor clams, thawed with their juice

steps.title: Render the bacon
steps.text: Cook the bacon in the pot over medium heat until crisp. Remove it and set it aside, leaving the fat in the pot.

steps.title: Sauté the vegetables
steps.text: Cook the onion and celery in the bacon fat until soft, about 5 minutes, adding the garlic for the last 30 seconds.

steps.title: Make the roux
steps.text: Sprinkle in the flour and stir constantly so it coats the vegetables and cooks out the raw flour taste.

steps.title: Add liquid and potatoes
steps.text: Slowly whisk in the clam juice to avoid lumps. Add the potatoes, thyme and bay leaf, and simmer gently until the potatoes are tender.

steps.title: Add the dairy
steps.text: Remove the thyme sprig and bay leaf. Stir in the cream and milk, and warm gently without letting it boil.

steps.title: Add the clams
steps.text: Stir in the clams with their juice and cook just until opaque. Any longer and they turn rubbery.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Taste first, since the clam juice is already salty. Add the black pepper and a splash of hot sauce or lemon if you like, then top with the crisp bacon.

notes: Freeze clams flat in portion-size bags with any juice from shucking, and thaw overnight in the fridge.
For thicker chowder, mash a few potatoes against the side of the pot before adding the dairy.
